changes.text: 还需要四个人。队长决定征求志愿者，同时写明：他心里其实基本知道会选谁——「I pretty well knew which of the people I would select」。他召集众人，说明计划，征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来。克林（Crean）原本被安排留在岛上当怀尔德的帮手，他恳求随行，与怀尔德商量之后，队长答应带上他。记述里也写了挑人的考虑：有人不够强壮，担不动船上的活；有人不是熟练水手，在船上派不上用场。

Four more were needed. He decided to call for volunteers while noting that he already had a pretty good idea of his choices — "I pretty well knew which of the people I would select". He called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers; many came forward at once. Crean had been slated to stay behind as Wild's right-hand man, but he begged so hard for a place in the boat that, after consulting Wild, the leader promised to take him. The account also sets out his criteria: some were not fit for the work the boat would demand, and others, not seasoned sailors, would be of little use aboard.
两位医生麦基尔罗伊（McIlroy）和麦克林（Macklin）都想随行，但明白自己的职责是留在岛上照顾病号。两位医生提议把双脚冻伤的布莱克博罗（Blackborrow）带上船，让他尽快得到温暖和庇护。队长否掉了这个提议。记录里给的理由是存活推断：健康的人在船上都难活；他看不出一个躺在舱底、动弹不得的病人，怎么可能熬过必定会遇到的坏天气。

The two doctors, McIlroy and Macklin, were both anxious to go but realized that their duty lay on the island with the sick men. The doctors suggested taking Blackborrow, the man with the frostbitten feet, so that he could have shelter and warmth as quickly as possible. The leader vetoed it. The record gives survival reasoning: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and he did not see how a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could possibly survive the heavy weather they were sure to encounter.

航程中有一次，遇上了队长二十六年海上经历中从未见过的巨浪，与多日来那些白浪翻卷的大浪完全不同。他高喊大家抓紧。船被像软木塞一样抛起、向前甩出，灌进半船水，在重击下颤抖；所有人拼命用随手抓到的容器掏水，十分钟后才觉得船重新有了生命。文森特在过去一周已不再是积极的船员，队长写明难以解释他的垮掉——他是船上体格最强壮的人之一，年轻，在北海拖网船上干过，本该比麦卡锡更能吃苦，而麦卡锡没那么强壮，却总是乐呵呵的。淡水减到每人每天半品脱。带上船的冰块早已用完，装船时一只水桶在浪里被撞裂，渗进了一些海水，喝的水发咸，渴得更厉害；队长不肯增加配给，有人恳求预支第二天的水，也被拒绝：万一风向不利，船可能被吹离海岛，航程拖长许多天。原文感叹，缺水是人所能承受的最严酷的匮乏。5月8日中午12点30分，麦卡锡从云隙中望见南乔治亚的黑色悬崖，距离开象岛整十四天。但岩岸看似直落入海，夜色将近，天气征兆也不好，那时贸然登陆无异自杀，只能离岸停驶，等待天亮。次日清晨风向转为西北，迅速增强为他们所有人经历过的最猛的飓风之一，风浪把船推向海岸，他们无能为力。直到天黑后风向突然转变，他们才得以重新驶离海岸；大风刚缓，锁住桅杆的销钉就掉了出来——队长写道，飓风中它若脱落，谁也救不了他们。5月10日，他们驶向一处队长认为必定是哈康国王湾（King Haakon Bay）的大海湾；风向转为从湾内吹出，他们在强风中抢风五次，才穿过礁石进入宽阔的湾口。暮色将近，他们转向海湾南岸一处有礁石护着的小湾。小船乘着涌浪触到海滩，几分钟后众人都平安上了岸；他们在脚边发现一条淡水溪流，随即跪下大口痛饮。但上岸并不等于求援成功：冰川和陡峭的山坡挡住了从小湾进入内陆的路，他们还得驶向海湾顶端，而指望找到捕鲸人的捕鲸站在东岸。

At one point came a wave beyond anything the leader had met in twenty-six years at sea — a mighty upheaval of the ocean, quite apart from the white-capped seas that had been their tireless enemies for many days. He shouted for everyone to hold on: "It's got us!" The boat was lifted and flung forward like a cork, half-full of water and shuddering under the blow; the men baled with the energy of men fighting for life, and after ten minutes of uncertainty felt her renew her life beneath them. Vincent had for the past week ceased to be an active member of the crew, and the leader could not easily account for his collapse: physically one of the strongest men in the boat, young, with service on North Sea trawlers, he should have borne hardship better than McCarthy, who was not so strong but always happy. The daily water allowance was cut to half a pint a man. The lumps of ice taken aboard were long gone, and the breaker had been slightly stove in during loading, letting in some sea-water, so the brackish water sharpened the thirst; the leader would not raise the allowance or let anyone draw against the morrow's, however he was begged — should the wind turn unfavourable, it might drive them away from the island and lengthen the voyage by many days. Lack of water, the account adds, is the severest privation men can be condemned to endure. At 12.30 p.m. on May 8, McCarthy caught a glimpse of the black cliffs of South Georgia through a rift in the clouds, just fourteen days after leaving Elephant Island. But the rocky coast seemed to drop sheer to the sea, night was drawing near and the weather signs were unfavourable; to have attempted a landing then would have been suicidal, so they hauled off and hove to, waiting for dawn. Early the next morning the wind shifted to the north-west and quickly rose to one of the worst hurricanes any of them had ever experienced; wind and sea were driving them ashore, and they could do nothing. Only after dark did the wind suddenly shift and leave them free to make an offing again; almost as soon as the gale eased, the pin that locked the mast to the thwart fell out — had it gone during the hurricane, the leader writes, nothing could have saved them. On May 10 they made for a big indentation the leader thought must be King Haakon Bay; with the wind blowing out of the bay, they tacked five times in the strong wind before getting through the reef into the wide mouth of the bay. With dusk approaching, they turned toward a small cove guarded by a reef on the south side of the bay. The boat ran in on a swell and touched the beach, and in a few minutes they were all safe ashore; finding a stream of fresh water almost at their feet, they were soon down on their knees drinking. But landing was not the same as securing relief: glaciers and precipitous mountain slopes barred the way inland from the cove, they still had to sail to the head of the sound, and the whaling stations where whalers could be counted on lay on the east coast.

把这几个决定放在一起看，一种解释是：真正让这个方案说得出口的，是最坏情形那笔账。出海的人带一个月口粮，一个月到不了南乔治亚就必死无疑，而留下的人在冬天少了几张要吃饭的嘴；最坏情形被算成：也不会给留下的人增加风险。据作者序言，留在象岛的二十二人在那里勉强熬了四个半月，远超当初一个月内带援助返回的预期；本文不据此推出因果评价。本文推断，当所有选项都糟透时，人们愿意跟从的未必是更有希望的那条路，而可能是把代价算清楚、不把损失转嫁给同伴的那条路。

Read together, these decisions suggest one explanation: what made the plan speakable was the arithmetic of the worst case. The boat party carried a month's provisions; if they did not make South Georgia within the month, they were sure to go under. The men left behind would have fewer mouths to feed through the winter. The worst case was calculated as adding nothing to the risks of the men left on the island. According to the author's preface, the twenty-two men left on Elephant Island eked out a bare existence there for four and a half months, far beyond the hoped-for return with relief within a month; this piece draws no causal verdict from that. This piece infers that when every option is grim, people will follow not necessarily the more hopeful road, but the one that costs its losses honestly and does not shift them onto comrades.
拒绝病号上船那一条，读起来最不舒服，但记录里给的是存活推断，不是道德立场：健康的人在船上都难活，在他看来，重病躺舱底的人熬不过坏天气。本文推断，这种取舍的难处不在决定本身，而在它必须给出理由——两位医生提了建议，被否掉了，记述里写明了否决的理由。

The refusal of the sick man is the least comfortable paragraph to read, yet the record offers survival reasoning rather than a moral stance: fit men would find it hard enough to live in the boat, and in his view a sick man lying helpless in the bottom could not survive the heavy weather. This piece infers that the difficulty of such a trade-off lies less in the decision itself than in having to give reasons for it: the two doctors made a proposal, it was vetoed, and the account sets down why.
还有一处值得留意：记述说他决定征求志愿者，同时心里基本知道会选谁。原文写明，他召集众人、说明计划、征求志愿者，许多人当即站了出来；但最终的人选仍由他选定。本文提出的一种替代做法是直接点名，省掉征求的形式。一种解释是：先向全队说明计划、详细讲清危险和理由，再征求志愿，可能让名单读起来更像共识而不是指派。这只是一种解释，所引段落没有说明他为什么这样安排。

One more detail catches the eye: the account says he decided to call for volunteers while already having a pretty good idea of his choices. The original states that he called the men together, explained his plan and asked for volunteers, and that many came forward at once; yet the final selection was still his. One alternative this piece raises would have been simply to name names and skip the formality. One reading is that explaining the plan and arguing the dangers and reasons to the party in detail before asking for volunteers may make the list read as consensus rather than assignment. This is only one reading, and the passages quoted give no reason for the arrangement.
全文只有当事人一个史源（其事后的第一人称自述）；航程部分据其逐日简略笔记（多为距离、船位、天气）与回忆写成；对话与心理均为记述性内容，未必逐字，本文未对照其他当事人的记录核实；天数只用原文明确写出的出海第六天和离开象岛第十四天，日期照原文写5月8日、5月10日，所引片段未给公元年份，不做换算；距离、口粮、水的数字照原文写法；原文为扫描识别文本，个别字词有讹误，引文照原文。

The whole piece rests on a single source — one participant's first-person account written afterwards; the voyage section was written from scanty day-by-day notes (mostly distances, positions and weather) together with memory. Dialogue and psychology are reported rather than transcribed, need not be verbatim, and have not been checked here against other participants' accounts; the only day counts used are the sixth day out and the fourteenth day after leaving Elephant Island, as stated in the original, dates follow the original (May 8 and May 10), and the quoted passages give no calendar year, so none is supplied; distances, rations and water figures follow the original wording; the source is a scanned print in OCR, with individual words occasionally garbled, and quotations follow it as printed.
